import Mathlib.Analysis.SpecialFunctions.Log.Basic
import Mathlib.Tactic.Linarith
import Mathlib.Tactic.Positivity
import Mathlib.Tactic.NoncommRing
import Mathlib.Tactic.Group
import Mathlib.Tactic.FieldSimp
import Mathlib.Tactic.Ring
import Mathlib.Tactic.Abel
import Mathlib.Algebra.Order.Archimedean.Basic
import Mathlib.Algebra.BigOperators.Group.Finset.Basic
import Mathlib.Data.Int.Order.Units
import Mathlib.Tactic.GCongr
open BigOperators

namespace YM

def gaugeTransform {G X : Type*} [Group G] (g : X → G) (U : X → X → G) : X → X → G :=
  fun x y => g x * U x y * (g y)⁻¹

structure Plaquette (X : Type*) where
  a : X
  b : X
  c : X
  d : X

def holonomy {G X : Type*} [Group G] (U : X → X → G) (p : Plaquette X) : G :=
  U p.a p.b * U p.b p.c * U p.c p.d * U p.d p.a

end YM
open YM

targets.name: jacobi_ring
targets.about: Jacobi identity for commutators. Algebra behind the Bianchi identity.
targets.statement: theorem jacobi_ring {R : Type*} [Ring R] (a b c : R) : (a * (b * c - c * b) - (b * c - c * b) * a) + (b * (c * a - a * c) - (c * a - a * c) * b) + (c * (a * b - b * a) - (a * b - b * a) * c) = 0

targets.name: holonomy_gauge
targets.about: Wilson loop around a plaquette transforms by conjugation. Core of lattice gauge invariance.
targets.statement: theorem holonomy_gauge {G X : Type*} [Group G] (g : X → G) (U : X → X → G) (p : Plaquette X) : holonomy (gaugeTransform g U) p = g p.a * holonomy U p * (g p.a)⁻¹

targets.name: two_site_gap
targets.about: Two-site lattice: on states orthogonal to the vacuum (1,1), energy is at least 2. A finite-volume gap.
targets.statement: theorem two_site_gap (v₀ v₁ : ℝ) (h : v₀ + v₁ = 0) : (v₀ - v₁) ^ 2 ≥ 2 * (v₀ ^ 2 + v₁ ^ 2)

targets.name: three_site_gap
targets.about: Complete graph on 3 sites: gap 3 above the vacuum.
targets.statement: theorem three_site_gap (v₀ v₁ v₂ : ℝ) (h : v₀ + v₁ + v₂ = 0) : (v₀ - v₁) ^ 2 + (v₁ - v₂) ^ 2 + (v₂ - v₀) ^ 2 ≥ 3 * (v₀ ^ 2 + v₁ ^ 2 + v₂ ^ 2)

targets.name: massive_uniform_gap
targets.about: Lattice free field WITH a mass term: gap ≥ m² for every lattice size N. Uniform in N, which is what a mass gap means.
targets.statement: theorem massive_uniform_gap (N : ℕ) (v : ℕ → ℝ) (m : ℝ) : ∑ i ∈ Finset.range N, (v (i + 1) - v i) ^ 2 + m ^ 2 * ∑ i ∈ Finset.range N, v i ^ 2 ≥ m ^ 2 * ∑ i ∈ Finset.range N, v i ^ 2

targets.name: gaps_can_close
targets.about: Positive gap at every size does not give a uniform gap.
targets.statement: theorem gaps_can_close : ∃ Δ : ℕ → ℝ, (∀ L, 0 < Δ L) ∧ ¬ ∃ m > 0, ∀ L, m ≤ Δ L

targets.name: massless_gap_closes
targets.about: STRETCH. Massless lattice field: mean-zero, unit-norm states with arbitrarily small gradient energy exist. The gap closes as N grows, so no mass gap. Contrast with massive_uniform_gap. Yang-Mills is classically massless; the conjecture is that quantum effects reopen the gap.
targets.statement: theorem massless_gap_closes : ∀ ε > 0, ∃ N : ℕ, ∃ v : ℕ → ℝ, (∑ i ∈ Finset.range N, v i = 0) ∧ (∑ i ∈ Finset.range N, v i ^ 2 = 1) ∧ ∑ i ∈ Finset.range (N - 1), (v (i + 1) - v i) ^ 2 < ε

targets.name: gap_criterion_discrete
targets.about: Conditional gap criterion, discrete spectrum: one common exponential rate for the heat kernel forces every occupied level above that rate. The finite-dimensional core of the reduction used against ChallengeSpec.
targets.statement: theorem gap_criterion_discrete (lam w : ℕ → ℝ) (n : ℕ) (hw : ∀ i, 0 ≤ w i) (C m : ℝ) (h : ∀ t : ℝ, 1 ≤ t → ∑ i ∈ Finset.range n, w i * Real.exp (-t * lam i) ≤ C * Real.exp (-m * t)) : ∀ i < n, 0 < w i → m ≤ lam i

targets.name: contraction_decay
targets.about: Transfer matrix contraction: a one-step contraction factor q gives geometric decay.
targets.statement: theorem contraction_decay (v : ℕ → ℝ) (q : ℝ) (hq : 0 ≤ q) (h : ∀ n, v (n + 1) ≤ q * v n) : ∀ n, v n ≤ q ^ n * v 0

targets.name: gap_from_contraction
targets.about: A contraction q < 1 at Euclidean time τ gives a positive gap -log(q)/τ.
targets.statement: theorem gap_from_contraction (q τ : ℝ) (hq : 0 < q) (hq1 : q < 1) (hτ : 0 < τ) : 0 < -Real.log q / τ

targets.name: pow_eq_exp_log
targets.about: Geometric decay is exponential decay with rate -log q.
targets.statement: theorem pow_eq_exp_log (q : ℝ) (hq : 0 < q) (n : ℕ) : q ^ n = Real.exp ((n : ℝ) * Real.log q)

targets.name: scale_split_uniform_gap
targets.about: Shape of RG-plus-strong-coupling arguments: a uniform bound beyond some scale plus positivity at the finitely many scales before it gives a uniform gap.
targets.statement: theorem scale_split_uniform_gap (Δ : ℕ → ℝ) (hpos : ∀ L, 0 < Δ L) (m : ℝ) (hm : 0 < m) (L₀ : ℕ) (h : ∀ L ≥ L₀, m ≤ Δ L) : ∃ m' > 0, ∀ L, m' ≤ Δ L

targets.name: polymer_series_bound
targets.about: Toy cluster expansion: small activity makes the polymer series converge with an explicit bound.
targets.statement: theorem polymer_series_bound (z : ℝ) (hz : |z| < 1) (N : ℕ) : ∑ n ∈ Finset.range N, |z| ^ n ≤ 1 / (1 - |z|)

targets.name: poincare_variance_decay
targets.about: Discrete Poincaré-to-decay step: if variance shrinks by a factor (1 - λ) per step, it decays exponentially.
targets.statement: theorem poincare_variance_decay (V : ℕ → ℝ) (lam : ℝ) (hl0 : 0 ≤ lam) (hl1 : lam ≤ 1) (h : ∀ n, V (n + 1) ≤ (1 - lam) * V n) : ∀ n, V n ≤ (1 - lam) ^ n * V 0

targets.name: holonomy_gauge_abelian
targets.about: Abelian (e.g. Z2, U(1)) gauge theory: plaquette holonomy is exactly gauge invariant, not just up to conjugation.
targets.statement: theorem holonomy_gauge_abelian {G X : Type*} [CommGroup G] (g : X → G) (U : X → X → G) (p : Plaquette X) : holonomy (gaugeTransform g U) p = holonomy U p

targets.name: z2_link_square
targets.about: Z2 links square to one, so the Wilson weight of a Z2 plaquette takes only two values.

_phase3_example.note: Phase 3: after adding OpenAI-YM-20261028 as a dependency of your Lean project, set preamble to import its ChallengeSpec and add a mass gap statement written against its definitions as a depth-0 target with pathway 1. Pin Lean to that repo's version.

induction n with
| zero => simp
| succ n ih => nlinarith [h n, ih, pow_succ q n]
